verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle, not from people nor through a person, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead,
verses.1:2: and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
verses.1:3: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.1:4: who gave Himself for our sins so that He might rescue us out of the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
verses.1:5: to whom belongs the glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1:6: I am astonished that you are so quickly turning away from the One who called you in the grace of Christ to a different gospel,
verses.1:7: which is not another; only there are some who are unsettling you and wanting to distort the gospel of Christ.
verses.1:8: But even if we or an angel from heaven should proclaim to you a gospel contrary to what we proclaimed to you, let him be accursed.
verses.1:9: As we have said beforehand, now I say again: if anyone is proclaiming to you a gospel contrary to what you received, let him be accursed.
verses.1:10: For am I now trying to win over people, or God? Or am I seeking to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be a slave of Christ.
verses.1:11: For I make known to you, brothers, that the gospel proclaimed by me is not human in origin;
verses.1:12: for neither did I receive it from a human, nor was I taught it, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.1:13: For you heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how beyond measure I was persecuting the church of God and ravaging it,
verses.1:14: and I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my own people, being far more zealous for my ancestral traditions.
verses.1:15: But when the One who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me through His grace was pleased
verses.1:16: to reveal His Son in me, so that I might proclaim Him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood,
verses.1:17: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away to Arabia and returned again to Damascus.
verses.1:18: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to become acquainted with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
verses.1:19: But I did not see any other of the apostles, except James, the Lord's brother.
verses.1:20: Now regarding what I am writing to you, look, before God, I am not lying.
verses.1:21: Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
verses.1:22: And I was unknown by face to the churches of Judea that are in Christ;
verses.1:23: they only kept hearing, "The one who once persecuted us is now proclaiming the faith that he formerly ravaged,"
verses.1:24: and they kept glorifying God on account of me.
verses.2:1: Then after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along as well.
verses.2:2: I went up in accordance with a revelation, and I laid before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles—privately, however, to those of repute—in case I might somehow be running, or had run, in vain.
verses.2:3: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, though he was a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.
verses.2:4: But because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who slipped in to spy out our freedom that we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might enslave us—
verses.2:5: to whom we did not yield in submission even for an hour, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.
verses.2:6: Now from those who were reputed to be something—whatever they once were makes no difference to me; God does not judge by a person's outward appearance—for those of repute added nothing to me,
verses.2:7: but on the contrary, seeing that I had been entrusted with the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised—
verses.2:8: for the One who worked effectively in Peter for an apostleship to the circumcised also worked effectively in me for the Gentiles—
verses.2:9: and recognizing the grace that had been given to me, James and Cephas and John, who were reputed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised;
verses.2:10: only that we should remember the poor, the very thing I was also eager to do.
verses.2:11: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.
verses.2:12: For before certain people came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, fearing those of the circumcision.
verses.2:13: And the rest of the Jews also joined him in hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.
verses.2:14: But when I saw that they were not walking straight in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of everyone, "If you, being a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how is it that you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
verses.2:15: We are Jews by nature and not sinners from among the Gentiles,
verses.2:16: yet knowing that a person is not justified by works of the law except through faith in Jesus Christ, we too believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no flesh will be justified.
verses.2:17: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? May it never be!
verses.2:18: For if I rebuild the very things that I tore down, I demonstrate myself to be a transgressor.
verses.2:19: For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ;
verses.2:20: yet I no longer live, but Christ lives in me; and the life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself over for me.
verses.2:21: I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
verses.3:1: O senseless Galatians, who bewitched you, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was publicly displayed as crucified?
verses.3:2: This alone I want to learn from you: Did you receive the Spirit from works of the law or from the hearing of faith?
verses.3:3: Are you so senseless? Having started by the Spirit, are you now being brought to completion by the flesh?
verses.3:4: Did you experience so many things in vain—if indeed it truly was in vain?
verses.3:5: Therefore, the One who supplies the Spirit to you and works miracles among you—does He do so from works of the law or from the hearing of faith?
verses.3:6: Just as Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.
verses.3:7: Know then that those who are of faith, these are sons of Abraham.
verses.3:8: And the Scripture, foreseeing that God justifies the nations by faith, announced the good news beforehand to Abraham: "In you all the nations will be blessed."
verses.3:9: Consequently, those who are of faith are blessed together with believing Abraham.
verses.3:10: For as many as are from works of the law are under a curse, for it is written, "Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all the things written in the book of the law, to do them."
verses.3:11: Now that no one is justified before God by the law is evident, for "The righteous one will live by faith."
verses.3:12: Yet the law is not of faith; rather, "The one who does them will live in them."
verses.3:13: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, becoming a curse on our behalf, because it is written, "Cursed is everyone hanging on a tree,"
verses.3:14: so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the nations in Christ Jesus, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
verses.3:15: Brothers, I am speaking in human terms: even a ratified human covenant no one annuls or adds provisions to.
verses.3:16: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, "And to seeds," as of many, but as of one, "And to your seed," who is Christ.
verses.3:17: Now this is what I say: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise.
verses.3:18: For if the inheritance is from the law, it is no longer from a promise; yet God has graciously granted it to Abraham through a promise.
verses.3:19: Why then the law? It was added on account of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom it had been promised, having been ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
verses.3:20: Now a mediator is not of one, yet God is one.
verses.3:21: Is the law then against the promises of God? May it never be! For if a law had been given that was able to impart life, then righteousness would indeed have been from the law.
verses.3:22: Instead, the Scripture confined everything under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
verses.3:23: Now before faith came, we were guarded under the law, being confined for the faith that was about to be revealed.
verses.3:24: So then, the law has become our custodian until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
verses.3:25: Now since faith has come, we are no longer under a custodian.
verses.3:26: For all of you are sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:27: For as many as were baptized into Christ, you have clothed yourselves with Christ.
verses.3:28: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free person, there is not male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:29: And if you belong to Christ, then you are the seed of Abraham, heirs according to promise.
verses.4:1: Now I say that as long as the heir is a child, he does not differ at all from a slave, though he is master of everything;
verses.4:2: rather, he is under guardians and stewards until the time appointed by the father.
verses.4:3: In the same way we also, when we were children, were enslaved under the elemental things of the world.
verses.4:4: But when the fullness of the time arrived, God sent out His Son, born from a woman, born under the law,
verses.4:5: so that He might redeem those who were under the law, in order that we might receive the adoption as sons.
verses.4:6: And because you are sons, God sent out the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, "Abba, Father!"
verses.4:7: So then, you are no longer a slave but a son; and if a son, also an heir through God.
verses.4:8: However, at that time, not knowing God, you were enslaved to those that by nature are not gods.
verses.4:9: But now, having come to know God—or rather, having been known by God—how are you turning back again to the weak and poor elemental things, to which you desire to be enslaved all over again?
verses.4:10: You are scrupulously observing days and months and seasons and years.
verses.4:11: I am afraid for you, that perhaps I have labored for you in vain.
verses.4:12: Become as I am, for I also became as you are, brothers, I plead with you. You did me no wrong;
verses.4:13: and you know that it was because of a weakness of the flesh that I preached the good news to you the first time,
verses.4:14: and your trial in my flesh you did not despise or spurn; instead, you welcomed me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
verses.4:15: Where then is that blessedness of yours? For I testify to you that, if it had been possible, you would have gouged out your eyes and given them to me.
verses.4:16: Therefore, have I become an enemy of yours by speaking the truth to you?
verses.4:17: They eagerly seek you, not in a good way, but they want to shut you out, so that you will eagerly seek them.
verses.4:18: Yet it is good to be eagerly sought for a good purpose at all times, and not only when I am present with you,
verses.4:19: my children, with whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you.
verses.4:20: And I wish I could be present with you right now and change my tone, because I am at a loss concerning you.
verses.4:21: Tell me, you who want to be under the law: do you not hear the law?
verses.4:22: For it is written that Abraham had two sons: one from the slave woman and one from the free woman.
verses.4:23: Yet the one from the slave woman was born according to the flesh, while the one from the free woman was born through promise.
verses.4:24: Now these things are spoken allegorically: for these women are two covenants—one from Mount Sinai, bearing children into slavery, which is Hagar.
verses.4:25: Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and she corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery together with her children.
verses.4:26: But the Jerusalem above is free; she is our mother.
verses.4:27: For it is written, "Be glad, barren woman who does not give birth; burst forth and shout, you who have no labor pains; because the children of the desolate woman are many more than those of the woman who has a husband."
verses.4:28: Now as for you, brothers, just like Isaac, you are children of promise.
verses.4:29: Yet just as at that time the one born according to the flesh kept persecuting the one born according to the Spirit, so it is now as well.
verses.4:30: But what does the Scripture say? "Drive out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman will certainly not inherit along with the son of the free woman."
verses.4:31: For this reason, brothers, we are not children of a slave woman, but of the free woman.
verses.5:1: For freedom Christ set us free; therefore stand firm, and do not again be held in a yoke of slavery.
verses.5:2: Look, I, Paul, tell you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will not benefit you at all.
verses.5:3: And I testify again to every man who lets himself be circumcised that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
verses.5:4: You have been cut off from Christ, you who are trying to be justified by law; you have fallen away from grace.
verses.5:5: For by the Spirit, from faith, we eagerly await the hope of righteousness.
verses.5:6: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any force, but faith active through love.
verses.5:7: You were running well; who obstructed you from obeying the truth?
verses.5:8: This persuasion is not from the One calling you.
verses.5:9: A small amount of leaven leavens the entire lump of dough.
verses.5:10: I have confidence in you in the Lord that you will think no other way; but the one troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
verses.5:11: But I, brothers, if I still proclaim circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the stumbling block of the cross has been nullified.
verses.5:12: I wish that those upsetting you would even castrate themselves.
verses.5:13: For you were called to freedom, brothers; only do not use that freedom as an occasion for the flesh, but through love be slaves to one another.
verses.5:14: For the entire law has been fulfilled in a single saying, in this: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
verses.5:15: But if you are biting and devouring one another, watch that you are not consumed by one another.
verses.5:16: Now I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will certainly not fulfill the desire of the flesh.
verses.5:17: For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these stand in opposition to one another, so that you do not do the things you wish.
verses.5:18: But if you are being led by the Spirit, you are not under law.
verses.5:19: Now the works of the flesh are plain, which are sexual immorality, impurity, debauchery,
verses.5:20: idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousies, outbursts of rage, selfish ambitions, dissensions, factions,
verses.5:21: envies, drunken bouts, carousings, and things similar to these, about which I forewarn you, just as I told you beforehand, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
verses.5:22: Now the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
verses.5:23: gentleness, self-control; there is no law against such things.
verses.5:24: Now those belonging to Christ Jesus crucified the flesh together with its passions and desires.
verses.5:25: If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk in line with the Spirit.
verses.5:26: Let us not become conceited, challenging one another, envying one another.
verses.6:1: Brothers, even if a person is overtaken in some trespass, you who are spiritual, restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, keeping watch on yourself, so that you also may not be tempted.
verses.6:2: Bear one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
verses.6:3: For if someone thinks himself to be something while being nothing, he deceives himself.
verses.6:4: But let each person test his own work, and then he will have his ground for boasting in regard to himself alone and not in regard to the other.
verses.6:5: For each person will bear his own load.
verses.6:6: Now let the one who is instructed in the word share in all good things with the one who instructs.
verses.6:7: Do not be misled: God is not mocked; for whatever a person sows, that he will also reap.
verses.6:8: Because the one sowing to his own flesh will reap decay from the flesh, but the one sowing to the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
verses.6:9: And let us not lose heart in doing what is good, for at the proper time we will reap if we do not grow faint.
verses.6:10: So then, as we have opportunity, let us do what is good toward all people, and especially toward those belonging to the household of the faith.
verses.6:11: See with what large letters I have written to you with my own hand.
verses.6:12: As many as want to make a fine impression in the flesh, these compel you to be circumcised, only so that they will not be persecuted because of the cross of Christ.
verses.6:13: For not even those who have been circumcised keep the law themselves, yet they want you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh.
verses.6:14: As for me, may I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
verses.6:15: For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything, but a new creation.
verses.6:16: And as many as will walk in line with this rule, peace be upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
verses.6:17: From this point on, let no one give me trouble, for I bear the brand marks of Jesus in my body.
verses.6:18: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

notes.1:3: The Greek text places 'our' with 'Lord Jesus Christ' rather than 'God the Father' (other manuscripts read 'God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ').
notes.1:6: Paul uses two Greek words for 'other' across verses 6-7: heteros ('different,' v. 6) and allos ('another,' v. 7).
notes.1:12: The phrase 'a revelation of Jesus Christ' can denote either a revelation given by Jesus Christ (subjective genitive) or a revelation disclosing Jesus Christ (objective genitive; compare 1:16).
notes.1:15: This Greek text omits 'God' before 'the One who set me apart,' leaving the divine subject implied (other manuscripts explicitly supply 'God').
notes.2:4: Paul's sentence breaks off grammatically across verses 4-5, reflecting his forceful refusal to concede to the false brothers regarding Titus's circumcision.
notes.2:14: Because the Greek text lacks quotation marks, interpreters debate whether Paul's spoken rebuke of Cephas concludes at verse 14 or extends through verse 21.
notes.2:16: The Greek phrases rendered 'faith in Jesus Christ' and 'faith in Christ' (pistis Christou) are debated and may mean either faith directed toward Christ (objective genitive) or the faithfulness of Christ (subjective genitive).
notes.2:19: Following the critical Greek versification, 'I have been crucified with Christ' closes verse 19 rather than beginning verse 20 as in some traditional English translations.
notes.3:2: The Greek phrase rendered 'the hearing of faith' (akoes pisteos) can mean either 'hearing with faith' or 'the message that produces faith.'
notes.3:15: The Greek word diatheke ('covenant') can also denote a human last will or legal disposition, which Paul uses here as an analogy for God's unalterable covenant with Abraham.
notes.3:20: This compressed statement is widely debated; it is commonly read as contrasting the law, which involved a mediator representing multiple parties, with God's direct, unilateral promise.
notes.3:22: The Greek genitive pisteos Iesou Christou can be taken either objectively as 'faith in Jesus Christ' or subjectively as 'the faithfulness of Jesus Christ.'
notes.3:24: A paidagogos ('custodian') was a household slave who escorted and supervised a child until maturity; 'until Christ' (eis Christon) can also carry the directional sense 'leading to Christ.'
notes.4:3: The phrase ta stoicheia tou kosmou ('the elemental things of the world') is debated and may refer to rudimentary religious principles, basic elements of the universe, or cosmic spiritual powers.
notes.4:14: The verb exeptysate literally means 'spat out,' an ancient idiom expressing strong aversion or a gesture to ward off ill omen.
notes.4:25: The Greek places the neuter article to before Hagar, treating the name itself as a term linked to Mount Sinai in Arabia; some ancient manuscripts omit 'Hagar' here.
notes.4:28: The critical text reads 'you...are' (hymeis...este), addressing the Galatians directly, whereas some later manuscripts read 'we...are.'
notes.5:6: The participle energoumene may be read as middle ("active/working through love") or passive ("made effective through love").
notes.5:12: The verb apokopsontai literally means "cut themselves off," a pointed play on circumcision referring to castration or emasculation.
notes.5:20: The Greek text here reads the plural zeloi ("jealousies"), matching the surrounding plural vices, whereas some manuscripts read the singular zelos ("jealousy").
notes.5:22: The Greek noun pistis can mean either "faith" or "faithfulness"; in this list of moral virtues, "faithfulness" (trustworthiness) fits the context.
notes.6:2: Paul distinguishes "burdens" (bare, heavy weights) here from "load" (phortion, an individual pack or responsibility) in v. 5; the verb anaplerosete is future indicative ("you will fulfill"), though some manuscripts read an imperative.
notes.6:11: "Large letters" likely reflects Paul taking the pen for emphasis (or possibly poor eyesight), and egrapsa may be read as a simple past ("I have written") or an epistolary aorist ("I am writing").
notes.6:14: The masculine relative pronoun di hou may refer either to the cross ("through which") or to Christ ("through Whom").
notes.6:16: The conjunction kai ("and") before "upon the Israel of God" is debated: it may either equate the "Israel of God" with all who follow this rule ("even upon...") or designate believing Jews alongside Gentile believers ("and upon...").
